title: Mild Shrimp Tacos with Lime Slaw
subtitle: smoky-sweet seasoned shrimp in warm tortillas with a crunchy creamy lime slaw, ready in 25 minutes
imageAlt: Three soft tortillas filled with golden shrimp and creamy shredded slaw, with lime wedges, on a cream plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: 8 tacos: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Thaw frozen shrimp in the fridge overnight, or in a sealed bag in cold water 20–30 minutes.

steps.title: Slaw
steps.text: Juice 1 lime and cut the other in wedges. Stir the mayonnaise, 1 tbsp of the lime juice, sugar and salt together, then toss with the coleslaw mix.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Pat the shrimp very dry and toss with the paprika, cumin, garlic powder, salt and the rest of the lime juice.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook the shrimp in one layer 1½–2 minutes a side, until pink and opaque all through, 74°C (165°F).

steps.title: Warm the tortillas
steps.text: Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet 20 seconds a side, or wrapped in a damp towel in the microwave 30 seconds.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Fill each tortilla with slaw and shrimp, add a spoon of sour cream and serve with lime wedges.

fixIt.fix: They were overcooked. Pull them as soon as they turn opaque and curl into a loose C.
Toss it no more than 30 minutes before eating.
Warm them right before filling and keep them wrapped in a towel.

saleTip: Frozen raw shrimp drops to about $9.99 for 680 g at No Frills; buy two bags when it does.
swap: Cod or haddock: cut in strips, same seasoning, cook 2–3 minutes a side to 70°C (158°F).
leftovers: Best fresh. Cold leftover shrimp is great on a salad the next day.
doneness: Shrimp 74°C (165°F): pink and opaque all the way through (Health Canada, shellfish).
source: Based on tested shrimp taco methods (Food Network Canada, Budget Bytes): paprika-cumin seasoned shrimp seared quickly, a creamy lime cabbage slaw, warm flour tortillas. No chili or hot sauce.
prepAhead: Mix the slaw dressing up to 3 days ahead; toss with the cabbage just before eating.
Season the shrimp up to 30 minutes ahead; longer and the lime softens it.
reheat: Best cold on a salad; reheated shrimp turns rubbery. To reheat, warm briefly in a skillet over medium, 1–2 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Seasoned shrimp, plain slaw and sour cream; no cumin.

stepNotes.0: Basic: no sugar in the slaw.

addSteps.title: Mango salsa
addSteps.text: Toss the mango, avocado and red onion with a squeeze of lime and a pinch of salt, and spoon it over the tacos.

plating: 3 tacos standing in a row, leaning together.
Salsa on top, lime wedges on the side.
Sour cream in a little dish.

why.0-2: Sweet paprika and cumin give taco-truck flavour without any heat.
why.1-2: Lime in both the slaw and shrimp ties the tacos together.
why.1-0: Bagged coleslaw mix saves shredding and stays crunchy.

funFact: Fish and shrimp tacos are a Baja California tradition, popularised in the 1950s by street stands in Ensenada.

keeps.note: cooked shrimp only; the slaw wilts
